News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 12:26:58 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Talking Europe</category><title>Europe's crisis of discontent: Student and cost-of-living protests spread across EU</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/talking-europe/20261106-europe-s-crisis-of-discontent-student-and-cost-of-living-protests-spread-across-eu</link><description>
A growing wave of discontent is sweeping across Europe. What began in France as student protests over deteriorating school conditions, teacher shortages and an education system under pressure has quickly grown into something much bigger: a groundswell of discontent over the rising cost of living, unaffordable housing and struggling public services.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/28d69d38-d922-11f1-bb94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/PHOTO-DEBAT-EN-2.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/28d69d38-d922-11f1-bb94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/PHOTO-DEBAT-EN-2.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5efb6fa2-d6b0-11f1-909b-3551a7733bb3</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:48:49 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Jennifer BEN BRAHIM</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French 2027 presidential elections: Why Melenchon is a Gen Z favourite</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/french-2027-presidential-elections-why-melenchon-is-a-gen-z-favourite</link><description>
Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon is beloved by French youth, but also one of the country’s most controversial politicians. His encouragement of the youth protests sweeping through France months ahead of the presidential election has only made him more divisive. So, why is Melenchon a Gen Z favourite? FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young supporters to find out.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/29fed0fa-d9d5-11f1-accf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/New-TITLE.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/29fed0fa-d9d5-11f1-accf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/New-TITLE.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4c270b52-d9d5-11f1-8b28-5774d120281e</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:43:31 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Midterms over, Democrats eye wide-open 2028 White House race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-midterms-over-democrats-eye-wide-open-2028-white-house-race</link><description>
With the US midterms over, Democrats are turning to what could become one of their most crowded and unpredictable presidential primaries in decades, a 2028 contest ​likely to expose the party's divide over how to win back the White House. Despite their resounding victories on Tuesday, Democrats enter the 2028 campaign still divided over whether to tack to the center or move further left on issues ranging from healthcare and taxes to policing and foreign policy.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9833ed10-d9cd-11f1-9d98-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261106-111023-111206-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9833ed10-d9cd-11f1-9d98-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261106-111023-111206-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9d380d50-d9cd-11f1-a9ee-f9c68a1f5134</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:42:13 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Israel president to announce Sunday who will form new government</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-israel-president-to-announce-sunday-who-will-form-new-government</link><description>
Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, following post-election talks with all party leaders. 46 parliament members recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, while 67 backed his opponent Gadi Eisenkot. Seven lawmakers abstained.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ead5c768-d9c9-11f1-b93b-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-19a34eeb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ead5c768-d9c9-11f1-b93b-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-19a34eeb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b3618c9a-d9c9-11f1-a51a-8fbe1edd1a21</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:39:11 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US Republicans face reckoning after major midterm election defeat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-us-republicans-face-reckoning-after-major-midterm-election-defeat</link><description>
Following the Democrats' sweeping victory in Tuesday's US midterm elections, Republicans are facing a moment of reckoning. With Donald Trump now a "lame-duck" president, the party must find a way forward after a historic electoral setback. The GOP faces major questions about how to win back voters and who will lead the party, with the next presidential election just two years away.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef78f86e-d9cc-11f1-9ae3-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261106-110817-111007-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef78f86e-d9cc-11f1-9ae3-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261106-110817-111007-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4b82890-d9cc-11f1-a436-2dd9069d3a05</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:37:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

]]> <![CDATA[ 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars ]]> A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history.

The meteorite, named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found.

The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California.

"It was only after we started looking closely that we realized this meteorite is really unique,” research leader Yang Liu of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California said in the statement. "One of the paper’s reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars."

A Rosetta Stone for Mars

Unlike many Martian meteorites, Teghaza 001 contains a distinctive combination of igneous minerals and textures that preserve evidence of its complex history. Its mineral composition resembles materials observed in Mars' southern highlands by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

Although researchers can’t pinpoint exactly where the meteorite originated on Mars, they have identified 13 potential locations on the planet where it may have formed.

"This is really our first piece of Martian crust from a part of Mars we’ve never had a sample of before," team member Lee Saper, NASA’s Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley, said. "It records interactions of water and rock and maybe even an imprint of the Martian atmosphere as it was losing water."

The meteorite was initially identified as Martian based on its oxygen isotopes. To determine its age, scientists then examined tiny zircon crystals embedded in the rock. Using a specialized rubidium-strontium dating technique, researchers analyzed individual mineral grains on its surface, preserving it for future analysis.

The results revealed that Teghaza 001 was altered by water around 4.1 billion years ago, suggesting the rock itself formed even earlier. The mineral and chemical evidence points to a dynamic water cycle on ancient Mars, when liquid water interacted with the planet's crust and potentially left traces of its atmosphere as it gradually lost water.

Scientists believe further analysis of Teghaza 001 could reveal more about how water shaped the Martian surface and influenced the planet's evolution. The study also marks the first time researchers have used rubidium-strontium dating to analyze an ancient Martian meteorite, opening the door for the technique to be applied to other samples in the future.

"We've only scratched the surface," Liu concluded.

Their findings were published on Thursday (Oct. 29) in the journal Science. A separate study examining the meteorite's water content was published on June 10 in the journal Science Advances, offering additional insight into early Mars.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays ]]> Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate "Max Power" on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same.

Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity.

"We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk. The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit.

Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem.

"We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy."

To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment.

Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue.

"We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell.

After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes.

"Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. Half the size of the old ones and bringing 40% more power."

Each of the eight iROSAs and their mounting assemblies were delivered to the space station by SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft. Beginning in June 2021, four teams of two astronauts did as was done on Thursday to deploy each array. In addition to Kutryk and Menon's work on the 2A and 3B power channels, the spacewalkers included Shane Kimbrough of NASA and Thomas Pesquet of the European Space Agency for the 2B and 4B channels; Josh Cassada and Frank Rubio, both with NASA, on 3A and 4A in December 2022; and NASA's Steve Bowen and Woody Hoburg on 1A and 1B in June 2023.

The need for the iROSA augmentations was discovered by flight controllers when the space station's eight original arrays began to show degraded power output as they exceeded their 15-year design life. The iROSAs provide the additional electricity needed to support ISS operations through its retirement and controlled deorbit, which are currently scheduled to occur in late 2030.

"Congratulations to you all on your stellar work to finish the last of the roll-out solar arrays and the upgrades to the ISS power system that will take it to the end of its journey," said Stilwell, addressing Menon and Kutryk. "It is fitting that we just surpassed 26 years of constant human presence on the International Space Station, and you all showed us what the best of humanity looks like executing one of the most difficult and dangerous [things] humans do and making it look easy. Congratulations!"

Menon has now logged 33 hours and 30 minutes on four spacewalks, while Kutryk has tailed 14 hours and 10 minutes on two EVAs. Thursday's spacewalk was the 101st U.S. EVA at the International Space Station without a space shuttle being present and the 286th overall in support of ISS assembly, maintenance and upgrades. It was the ninth spacewalk of 2026 and the sixth conducted by the station's 75th resident crew.

]]> <![CDATA[ Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine ]]> Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger.

Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible.

The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today. "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [geostationary orbit] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space."

New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment. Its reusable first stage is powered by seven of Blue Origin's BE-4 engines, and its second stage features two of the company's BE-3Us. The rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall and can haul 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) to geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) and 50 tons (45 metric tons) to low Earth orbit (LEO).

These are the specs for the standard, or "7x2," version of New Glenn. Last year, Blue Origin announced that it's developing a super-heavy variant known as the 9x4, because it will feature nine first-stage BE-4s and four upper-stage BE-3Us. The 9x4 will be nearly 400 feet (122 m) tall, and it will be able to loft 15.4 tons (14 metric tons) to GTO and 77 tons (70 metric tons) to LEO, according to Blue Origin.

New Glenn has flown three times to date, each time in the 7x2 configuration. The rocket debuted in January 2025, then launched again in November 2025 and again on April 19 of this year.

Things didn't go according to plan on that latest mission. The rocket deployed AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 communications satellite into the wrong orbit, and the spacecraft ended up being lost.

Another setback came just a month later: On May 28, New Glenn exploded on the pad during a routine engine test at Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Blue Origin has been working ever since to rebuild the pad and get New Glenn ready for its fourth flight, which is expected to occur late this year.

We now know that Blue Origin has also been working on the GS3 while those repairs were underway. The new stage will be powered by one BE-7 engine, which the company developed for use on its Blue Moon spacecraft, one of the two private vehicles that NASA selected to be crewed lunar landers for its Artemis program. (The other is SpaceX's Starship.)

Blue Moon landing missions won't need to launch on GS3-equipped New Glenn rockets, according to Blue Origin. But the third stage "can support sustained operations around the moon," the company wrote in today's blog post. "By delivering significant payload mass directly to trans-lunar injection (TLI), GS3 enables faster transit times while preserving propellant for on-orbit operations."

And there's already demand for such services: Blue Origin also announced today that a government customer (which it did not name) has booked a GS3 mission to cislunar (Earth-moon) space, with launch targeted for 2028.

And the company dropped yet more news today — that it's working on a new first-stage engine, called Northstar.

Like Blue Origin's other booster engine, the BE-4, Northstar burns liquid oxygen and liquid methane propellant, a combination known as methalox. But the new engine is more powerful and less complex.

"Compared to the BE-4 engine, Northstar reduces mass by 30% and parts count by 50%, while increasing thrust from 640,000 to 715,000 pounds-force," Blue Origin said in a second blog post today. "Manufacturing advancements have also significantly shortened production timelines, enabling assembly in less than a day."

Northstar went from program approval to development testing in just 11 months, according to the company. But today's update did not say when the new engine will fly for the first time.

]]> <![CDATA[ Earth has captured a new mini moon  — but it won't stick around for long ]]> Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and it is sticking around for Christmas.

The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29).

The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027.

Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun. QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it.

According to the Minor Planet Center, the closest QQ8 will come to our planet during this stay is around 353,000 miles (568,000 kilometers). That is around 110,000 miles (177,000 km) further out than the average distance between Earth and the moon.

Even if QQ8 were to come close enough to collide with Earth, it would likely be completely destroyed in our planet's atmosphere before it reaches the surface, as it is only around 6 feet (2 meters) in diameter.

This is far from the first time Earth has snagged itself a mini-moon, more accurately called a temporary satellite. In fact, research last year suggested that our planet could be orbited by as many as six mini-moons at any given time, with many of these being fragments of our more permanent natural satellite, the moon.

While QQ8 is tiny, it is larger than the average mini-moon. That is according to modelling earlier this year that suggested the average size for a temporary satellite is 75 centimeters (30 inches) across.

The same modelling suggested the average stay for such an object would be around nine months.

So if QQ8 was captured in April 2026, that means it should move away in January 2027.

The researchers behind those findings suggested that, were Earth to gravitationally grip a space rock around 10 feet (3 meters) wide, it could serve as a mini-moon for 10 to 20 years.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 5, 2002: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by Jupiter moon Amalthea only to find it's a 'pile of icy rubble less dense than water' ]]>

On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft was almost out of fuel. But the Jupiter mission still had some science to do. Galileo flew by a small moon called Amalthea. Amalthea is small, but it's interesting for scientists.

The Jupiter moon Amalthea is the reddest object in our solar system. It also generates more heat than it gets from the sun. Scientists think Amalthea creates electrical currents as it orbits in Jupiter's huge magnetic field. Near this little moon, strong radiation from Jupiter is dangerous for spacecraft.

The flyby caused some problems for Galileo. The spacecraft went into safe mode only 30 minutes after going past Amalthea. NASA said it was ready for problems, because Galileo was on its last legs, and the radiation near Amalthea was strong. However, NASA quickly fixed the problem and got Galileo working again.

Less than a year later, Galileo threw itself into Jupiter's atmosphere. The spacecraft was crushed by the high pressure in Jupiter's atmosphere, but its data still survives on Earth.

Why it mattered

The Galileo spacecraft was running on cosmic fumes by the time it reached Amalthea and the flyby would be the last time the probe would ever swing by one of Jupiter's moons.

While it may not look like it in Galileo's black and white images above and below, Amalthea is tinted red due sulfur contamination on its surface. The moon is small, about 168 miles long, and orbits about 112,468 miles (181,000 km) from Jupiter (much closer to the planet than the Earth and its moon).

Galileo flew within 99 miles of Amalthea during its flyby, which also marked the closest Galileo would get to Jupiter before its death dive in September 2005.

"Scientists studying data from NASA's Galileo spacecraft have found that Jupiter's moon Amalthea is a pile of icy rubble less dense than water," NASA announced in May 2005

"Amalthea is throwing us a curve ball," Torrence Johnson, a study co-author on the Almathea flyby and project scientist for the Galileo mission at JPL, said in 2005. "Its density is well below that of water ice, and even with substantial porosity, Amalthea probably contains a lot of water ice, as well as rock."

Originally known as Jupiter V (because it was the fifth Jupiter moon discovered after the so-called Galilean moons Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto), Amalthea was named after naiad, or water nymph, from Greek mythology.

It is fitting that Amalthea was the last of Jupiter's moons to be visited by the Galileo spacecraft. The moon was also last Jupiter moon to be discovered by visual observations when it was first disovered by astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard in September 1892 using the Lick Observatory telescope in California.

The Galileo spacecraft ultimately crashed into Jupiter on Sept. 21, 2005, less than a year after its Amalthea flyby.

"The team has so far determined that one group of thrusters went offline and their backups turned on. Voyager 1 and its still-operational twin, Voyager 2, both launched in 1977 on an initial mission to explore planets in the solar system. The two spacecraft took advantage of a rare alignment that allowed them to swing from Jupiter to Saturn to Uranus and Neptune using a minimum of fuel, although funding to explore the more distant planets and moons was not guaranteed at launch.

The spacecraft duly swung by Jupiter's and Saturn's systems (some months apart from each other) to great acclaim before parting pathways. Voyager 1's close-up view of Saturn's rings as well as the moon Titan — which may have prebiotic or pre-life chemistry — altered the spacecraft's trajectory to put it high above the plane of the solar system. Meanwhile, Voyager 2 flew on to Uranus and Neptune in 1986 and 1989, respectively, providing the only up-close view of these planetary systems to date.

Running on nuclear power, and continuing to deliver valuable science from deep space, the Voyagers saw their missions extended repeatedly. Both crossed into interstellar space a few years ago, and are still operational.

But with age comes a cost: the plutonium power sources on both spacecraft are diminishing, requiring engineers to periodically shut off instruments or come up with other clever ways of saving power. Voyager 1 just underwent one of those power adjustments, nicknamed the "Big Bang" because it reconfigured a number of spacecraft instruments.

"In early September, engineers successfully turned off three devices on the Voyager 1 spacecraft and substituted them with three lower-power alternatives," JPL wrote of the effort, noting that Voyager 2 also had a "Big Bang" about six weeks previous to that.

Spacewalks are hard work, so sometimes you need to take a break for a moment and snap a gorgeous selfie with your home planet in the background.

What is it?

During a pre-Halloween spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk took a moment to pose for a photograph.

In this moment, the International Space Station to which he was tethered was orbiting 267 miles (430 kilometers) above the South Atlantic Ocean down below on Earth.

During this spacewalk — the first for a Canadian since 2019 — Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon worked together to install a new roll-out solar array on the station while also performing some "get ahead" tasks to prep for the next spacewalk, which is happening today (Nov. 5).

During today's excursion, the same two astronauts will venture out into space, tethered to the space station, to install the eighth and final roll-out solar array. These eight new arrays will boost the station's available power by a total of 30%, according to NASA officials.

Why is it incredible?

When we think of astronauts working in space, we might think of the important science and research they're doing aboard the station. Astronauts work on everything from biomedical research to plant science and physics experiments. But the job also includes work on the space station itself.

Sometimes they have to venture out into the vacuum of space to fix urgent problems. These situations can be tense, and there's a lot of pressure to get things absolutely right.

But even spacewalks that do relatively mundane maintenance work, like the one on Oct. 29, come with pressure. Every minute that astronauts spend outside of the space station, there are countless risk factors floating around. Earth orbit is a very harsh environment, after all, even if it does allow for some pretty amazing selfies.

   <description>Slunečné dny vystřídají mrazivá rána a na mnoha místech bude panovat i vytrvalá nízká oblačnost. Víkendové počasí v Česku ovlivní tlaková výše, která přinese stabilní oblohu, ale i riziko namrzajících silnic a mrznoucích mlh, na které by si měli dát pozor zejména řidiči. Příjemné denní teploty a sluneční paprsky ale dlouho nevydrží. Už v pondělí se začne počasí měnit. Od západu přibude oblačnosti a postupně by se měly přidat i srážky.</description>

   <description>Na bolesti v oblasti zad a krku si občas stěžuje takřka každý. Šíjové svaly kvůli neustálému hledění na mobil či práci na počítači totiž trápí i lidi, kteří dlouhodobé ani vážnější problémy s krční či hrudní páteří nemají.    <title>Black Friday ukrývá i falešné slevy. Jak odhalit triky obchodníků a nenaletět</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-ekonomika-black-friday-falesne-slevy/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Nákupní období kolem Black Friday v Česku naplno propuklo. Tradiční termín letos ve světě připadá na 27. listopadu, většina velkých online prodejců u nás však již své masivní slevové kampaně spustila. Spotřebitelské organizace varují před psychologickým nátlakem a triky e-shopů a poukazují i na blížící se velkou novinku u nákupů na internetu. Od roku 2027 začne se zpožděním platit takzvaná tlačítková novela. Zjednoduší zákazníkům vrácení zboží.</description>

Nyní skončil ve vazbě a hrozí mu dalších až pět let vězení.</description></item><item><title>Vyřazené sanitky z Libereckého kraje míří na Ukrajinu. Pomohou zachraňovat životy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/905055-vyrazene-sanitky-z-libereckeho-kraje-miri-na-ukrajinu-pomohou-zachranovat-zivoty.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/905055-vyrazene-sanitky-z-libereckeho-kraje-miri-na-ukrajinu-pomohou-zachranovat-zivoty.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:03:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Další tři sanitky, které dosud sloužily záchranářům v Libereckém kraji, zamíří na Ukrajinu. Kraj tak navazuje na loňskou pomoc, celkově daroval už osm těchto vozů.</description></item><item><title>Víkend bude slunečný, zaprší až příští týden</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905058-vikend-bude-slunecny-zaprsi-az-pristi-tyden.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905058-vikend-bude-slunecny-zaprsi-az-pristi-tyden.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Počasí v Libereckém kraji slibuje na víkend sice poměrně nízké teploty, ale slunečné počasí. ]]> Okresní kolo ČEPS Cupu – florbal 1. stupeň základních škol (kluci) 2026/2027 https://www.vybezek.eu/296441-okresni-kolo-ceps-cupu-florbal-1-stupen-zakladnich-skol-kluci-2026-2027/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:35:41 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296441 Ve středu 4. listopadu 2026 se ve Varnsdorfu ve sportovní hale hrál florbal, proběhlo okresní kolo ČEPS Cupu Děčín-Šluknovsko pro 1. stupeň základních škol (kluci).

Ve středu 4. listopadu 2026 se ve sportovní hale ve Varnsdorfu uskutečnilo okresní kolo florbalového turnaje ČEPS Cupu, určeného pro žáky 1.–5. tříd základních škol.

Turnaj se hrál systémem 3 + 1. Každý tým se utkal s každým soupeřem dvoukolově, přičemž jedno utkání trvalo 2 × 8 minut. Na turnaji se představily tři týmy – ZŠ Východní, Centrum dětí a mládeže Česká Kamenice a naše škola. Každý tým tak odehrál celkem čtyři utkání. Vítězný tým turnaje postoupí do krajského finále.

Hned v úvodním utkání nás čekal nejtěžší soupeř, domácí ZŠ Východní. Po velmi vyrovnaném a bojovném průběhu jsme dokázali zvítězit těsným výsledkem 4:3. Druhý zápas proti soupeři z České Kamenice jsme zvládli výborně a po přesvědčivém výkonu jsme zvítězili 6:2. Ve druhém kole jsme se znovu utkali se ZŠ Východní. Tentokrát nám soupeř porážku oplatil a po dramatickém průběhu jsme prohráli nejtěsnějším rozdílem 2:3. Jelikož i ZŠ Východní zvítězila nad Českou Kamenicí, bylo před závěrečným utkáním jasné, že o vítězi turnaje rozhodne počet vstřelených branek proti tomuto soupeři.

Do závěrečného utkání jsme proto nastoupili s jasnou taktikou – vstřelit co nejvíce branek. Po většinu turnaje nás v brance skvěle držel Adam Reichert, který několika výbornými zákroky podržel tým v nejtěžších chvílích. Pro rozhodující utkání jsme však zvolili odvážný taktický tah.
